title: Record each agent invocation's effort level; set it per role
summary: Add an effort level to every agent invocation: chosen per role (reader, producer, verifier, steward) from athena.toml, passed to Claude Code as `--effort`, and written into each `athena.invocation/1` record. The audience is the user and the scorer, who will compare effort with cost and outcome.

defaults_applied.how: New unit and fake-driver tests cover argument building, config validation and the record field. cargo test and clippy must be clean.
Criteria check that the flag reaches the driver arguments and that the effort appears in written records, not just that a field exists.
Config loading rejects a missing or unknown effort, so the rule is enforced and not left to prose.
One change covering config, driver and record. No tuning and no backfill.
The config comment and docs explain the effort choices for an outside reader.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check, and checks the fake-driver records.
Effort is set in one config-driven place for all roles, not patched into one call site.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Effort is a Claude Code setting, passed as `--effort <level>` with levels low, medium, high, xhigh, max. The worker is pinned at 2.1.301, so the producer must confirm that flag exists there from the repository's docs or notes; if it does not, the equivalent setting is used and the choice is documented.

The per-role choice lives in athena.toml under [models] or a new [effort] table, with a default per role (for example reader low, producer medium, verifier high). The values are my guess and the user can adjust them.
Roles are those in athena_data::records::Role (reader, producer, verifier, steward, and any others there). Each gets an effort, and a missing entry is a config error, not a silent default.

The record gains an optional `effort` field, serde-defaulted so existing records still parse. Old records show no effort and are not rewritten. The schema name stays athena.invocation/1 unless the repository's schema rules require a bump.
Fake-driver invocations record the effort they were given even though no model call happens.
athena.toml is a governance file and is changed by this job, so it is listed and named in a criterion. It governs only later jobs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. It passes. New tests show that `ClaudeDriver` argument building includes `--effort <level>` for the spec's effort, and that an invocation record built from a spec carries the same effort value.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`. Both are clean.

athena.toml sets an effort level for each role (reader, producer, verifier, plus steward if it is invoked), with a comment explaining the choice. Config loading rejects an unknown level or a missing role, and a test covers each rejection.

`AgentInvocation` in crates/athena-agent/src/lib.rs has an effort field. Every place that builds one (reading, run, manage and the like) fills it from the role's configured effort, not a hard-coded value.
The `athena.invocation/1` record in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs has an effort field. A test shows that a record JSON written before this change, with no effort field, still deserializes.
Run the fake-driver end-to-end tests with `cargo test`. The invocation records written for a reader, a producer and a verifier each contain that role's configured effort, and the three can differ.

The design docs (docs/design/athena-v0.md or the closest match) and CHANGELOG.md say where effort is configured, what is recorded, and why it differs by role. Any figure given is labeled as an estimate.

out_of_scope: Tuning effort from measured results. The job records effort and sets initial per-role values only.
Backfilling effort into existing records, which are never edited.
Changing the models, budgets or timeouts.
Upgrading the pinned Claude Code version, unless `--effort` turns out to need it. In that case the producer should report it, not do it.
Changing which model each role uses.
departures: This is a cross-crate change (config, driver, record schema and tests across about 8 files) that touches the governance file athena.toml and a record schema. That puts cost and time above the reference forecast and lowers the pass probability. The unconfirmed `--effort` flag in the pinned Claude Code version adds risk.
